messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT P1 — GPU pool queue growth detected in eu-west-1 (alert id: ALRT-20260315-47). Autoscaler attempted scale but pool stayed at max. Dashboard: https://redwood.app/d/infra/gpu-pools?panel=queue

maya: seeing it too. customer-facing latency spikes, some 503s. paging oncall.

ashwin: oncall here — joining. what scope? hosted api or dedicated?

maya: hosted API first, but looks like dedicated pools also affected for some tenants. queue depth per-pool jumped ~4x in 3m.

chris: grabbing metrics now. prefix_cache_miss_rate for request-id prefix namespace jumped to 78% around 2123456500. continuous_batch_window_ms seems to have been bumped in the last deploy from 20->200ms on 2026-03-15 02:45UTC.

laura: customer impact: multiple production customers in eu-west seeing 429/503 throttles, most common on streaming generation endpoints. support ticket spike: 14 new high-priority tickets in last hour.

oncall-rotation: assigning pager to ashwin. runbook: https://redwood.app/runbooks/gpu-exhaustion. please follow page steps 1-3.

ashwin: running quick checks — autoscaler logs show repeated scale attempts failing with "scale_limit_reached" for pool eu-west-1a. Policy max_nodes=40, current nodes=40. but queue still nonzero, so scaling isn't allowed. we need either manual capacity increase or fallbacks.

chris: adding recent deploy note: rollout 20260315-03 toggled "continuous_batch.enabled=true" and a cache config `prefix_cache.enabled=false` for a small experiment. config id cfg-9072. metric correlation looks strong.

maya: if prefix cache is off, we lose KV cache hit for prefixes causing massive recomputation and longer GPU holding times -> throughput collapse.

ashwin: attempting manual mitigation: requesting temporary node limit bump to 60 from infra. @engops-bot can you approve temporary capacity quota?

engops-bot: :white_check_mark: Request received. Approving emergency increase to 60 nodes for eu-west-1 for 2 hours. Provisioning...

chris: while infra scales, we should rollback cfg-9072 to re-enable prefix cache and restore batching window to 20ms. Rolling back will reduce per-request GPU time.

laura: agree — rollback will likely decrease queue faster than waiting for new nodes. customer comms: preparing status update for affected customers (EU-hosted) — i'll post in #support-alerts once we have ETA.

ashwin: executing rollback now: `redwoodctl config rollback --id cfg-9072 --env eu-west-1`

chris: logs from config service: 
```
INFO 2026-03-15T02:59:12Z rollback initiated cfg-9072 by ashwin
INFO 2026-03-15T02:59:18Z applying config to runtime clusters eu-west-1
WARN 2026-03-15T02:59:25Z streaming workers reconnecting
```

maya: watch prefix cache hit rate and per-gpu p50 latency.

ashwin: prefix_cache_hit_rate -> 1.2% -> 62% within 90s after rollback. continuous_batch_window_ms back to 20ms. queue depth dropping from 3200 -> 1200 in 6 minutes.

chris: autoscaler also reports pending node provisioning — infra increased quota to 60 and nodes are coming up. scaling events starting to succeed.

laura: posted customer update: "We're investigating elevated latencies in EU; mitigation in progress. ETA ~30m." #support-alerts :mailbox_with_mail:

oncall-rotation: good call on rollback. temporary quota increase will prevent immediate 503 spike while traffic normalizes. keep monitoring for 30m then re-evaluate.

maya: one residual issue — a small percentage of requests still hitting 503s due to token bucket throttler hitting per-route burst cap. I suggest a temporary route-level burst increase for streaming routes in eu-west.

chris: applied temp patch: `rbacctl update-route --route /v1/stream --burst 2000 --scope eu-west-1` — verify in 30s.

ashwin: post-patch checks: 503 rate down from 6.8% -> 0.9% over 10m window. overall CPU/GPU utilization now within expected envelope.

laura: support updated customers with "mitigation completed, monitoring, follow-up". Created incident ticket INC-20260315-47 and customer RCA follow-up task.

chris: root cause notes for later: recent config experiment disabled prefix cache and extended continuous batching window which unintentionally increased steady-state GPU hold time per request and reduced effective throughput, interacting badly with autoscaler max_nodes limit. Need guardrails: automated perf regression checks on config toggles and hard limits on continuous_batch_window_ms in prod.

maya: adding to backlog: (1) config-gate for prefix_cache toggles, (2) auto-revert if prefix_cache_hit_rate < 30% and p50 token latency increases > 40% in 5m, (3) autoscaler policy review for emergency headroom.

ashwin: closing pager, staying as incident lead for postmortem. next steps: timeline, metric snapshots, who merged cfg-9072, and change control.

incident-bot: Incident update: mitigated. Severity downgraded to P3. Incident ticket: https://redwood.app/incidents/INC-20260315-47. Please add postmortem notes within 48h. :lock_with_ink_pen:
